## Rounding pi

```{r}
round(3.1415926)
round(3.1415926, digits = 2)
```

## Argument order

```{r}
print(seq(3, 10, 2))
```

## Variable type

```{r}
b = TRUE
print(paste(class(b), b))

c = 'variable'
print(paste(class(c), c))

```

## Data with radiated cells

```{r}
cell_ID_1 = 'CX1'
cell_ID_2 = 'CX2'
treated_1 = TRUE
treated_2 = FALSE
num_cells_before_1 = 5415
num_cells_before_2 = 8123
num_cells_after_1 = 1432
num_cells_after_2 = 7543
```

## Weird R behaviours

```{r}
print(TRUE + TRUE)
print(TRUE + FALSE)
print(5 + TRUE)
```

Boolean variables in R can behave like numbers.
